title: A longer open pipe
hook: Change pipe length and predict fundamental frequency.
misconception: fundamental frequency doubles when pipe length doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply f₁ = v/(2L) to compare fundamental frequency when pipe length changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal pipe open at both ends with fixed sound speed, f₁ = v/(2L). When pipe length doubles, fundamental frequency becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f₁ = v/(2L); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal pipe open at both ends with fixed sound speed, with a nonzero initial result. If pipe length triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on fundamental frequency?
recall.why: Apply f₁ = v/(2L) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
